The qualification is the channel's nature: music channels can carry a child audience later than a general entertainment channel would, which is a matter for the reviewer rather than a rule-driven bar.

The binding eight-factor context definition, which is why the same material is a different answer at 22:15 and at 15:00 with no change to the work. The rule most specific to this content, and it does not bar a 22:15 showing on any reading - but its application needs stating carefully because it has three limbs. decisions.reasoning:
ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS FIRST, read for coverage rather than category label. UK-GEN-001 bars material that might SERIOUSLY impair the development of under-eighteens, with no contextual, scheduling or technical cure. 'Seriously impair' is a deliberately higher bar than ordinary harm, and a 1980s-style narrative horror music video with prosthetic effects is not in that tier: there is no violence, injury detail or blood recorded anywhere in the observations (the input is expressly silent on whether any exists), the material is fictional throughout, and the work carries a disclaimer disavowing endorsement of occult belief (o7). Provisional view: it does not bite. Judgment_based, so flagged. UK-SEX-001 (R18-equivalent material at any time) is not engaged: no sexual content is recorded at all. UK-FLM-006 (R18 films) is not engaged: no certificate. UK-FLM-001 (films refused BBFC classification) is not engaged, and the reasoning matters - 'CERTIFICATE: none' means no certificate was sought or recorded, which is categorically different from a refusal; reading an empty certificate field as a refusal would ban an ordinary music video outright.

ROUTING. is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no'. Two transmissions are recorded and they are DECIDED SEPARATELY, as the procedure requires: t1 the full video at 22:15, t2 the 30-second trailer at 15:00. The extractor expressly notes that the schema cannot link an observation to a transmission and states the mapping - o1 to o7 belong to the video, o8 to o10 to the trailer - and I have used that mapping rather than pooling all ten observations into one decision. Pooling them would have produced one averaged answer for two materially different slots, which is the error this case is built around.

SERVICE APPLICABILITY. service_type is not_stated and the observations record as unknown whether the music channel is free-to-air, subscription or access-controlled. I have branched and labelled rather than picking: general linear / free-to-air (21:00), premium subscription film without protection (20:00, a service type a music channel is unlikely to be), and any MDP-capable service (watershed disapplied). At 22:15 all three branches permit the showing, so the answer is robust to the unknown - which I state explicitly, because 'the missing fact does not change this particular answer' is a different and more useful statement than either resolving it by assumption or refusing to answer.

THE HOURS. 22:15 is past 21:00, so UK-SCH-002 is satisfied. The material that would have made a daytime slot wrong is recorded in detail - sustained prosthetic transformation (o1, o2), decayed faces shown in detail over an extended sequence (o3, o4), a pursuit ending in a woman cornered in a derelict house (o5), and a closing shot of non-human eyes (o6) - and it is fear-and-distress material rather than violence. Post-watershed, UK-DEF-003's context factors govern, and they are met on an ordinary view at 22:15 on a music channel.

THE OCCULT RULE, WHICH IS WHERE THIS CASE COULD GO WRONG IN EITHER DIRECTION. UK-OCC-001 has a deliberate three-way split. Over-application would bar the video because werewolves and risen corpses are plainly 'paranormal activity'; that is the category-label error, since the rule's first limb turns on PRESENTED AS REAL and this is fiction with an explicit disclaimer. Under-application would treat the fiction exemption as disposing of the rule entirely; that is also wrong, because the exemption names drama, film and comedy and a music video is none of those three words, and because the second limb - entertainment treatment, restricted by expected child audience rather than by the clock - would survive the exemption's absence. At 22:15 both limbs are satisfied however the exemption question is resolved, so I clear the slot and flag the enumeration question rather than resting the clearance on it.

FEAR AND DISTRESS. UK-SCH-005 requires clear information about content that may distress some children, if appropriate and taking account of context; its verbatim quote is framed on programmes broadcast BEFORE the watershed, so it does not impose a duty at 22:15. It is the rule that does real work on the trailer.

CONTEXT FACTORS THAT ARE OPEN BUT DO NOT CHANGE THE ANSWER. The date is not stated, so neither the school-holiday factor [UK-SCH-010] nor the cultural or religious calendar [UK-SCH-011] can be applied; both change who is watching without changing the clock, and at 22:15 neither is likely to be decisive. UK-CTX-010 records that audience size can make a decision stricter but never looser, so a music channel cannot argue for latitude from being niche. UK-SCH-006's cumulative-effect and repeat-scheduling points are relevant if this showing recurs, which is unknown.

CONFLICTS. None arose. UK-SCH-007 (rank 1) would displace UK-SCH-002 only if MDP were in place; it is not claimed, and the answer does not need it.

DETERMINACY AND ESCALATION. UK-SCH-002 is bright_line and 22:15 passes it mechanically. But the decision also rests on judgment_based rules - UK-SCH-001, UK-DEF-002, UK-DEF-003, UK-FLM-010, UK-SCH-004, UK-SCH-008, UK-SCH-010, UK-SCH-011, UK-CTX-010, UK-SCH-005, UK-WRN-002, UK-WRN-003, UK-GEN-001, UK-GEN-002 - and UK-OCC-001 is conditional on a classification of the treatment. Human review is required as a property of those rules. Confidence is medium rather than high: the hour is comfortably clear, but the service type, the date, the channel's audience profile and the occult-exemption question are all open.

A pre-watershed trailer may contain ONLY material appropriate for a pre-watershed audience, and the trailer as recorded contains the decayed faces from the graveyard sequence (o8, o9) and the pursuit cut FASTER than in the full video (o10) - that is, it concentrates the work's most distressing material into 30 seconds rather than diluting it. Two routes forward, both of which are the broadcaster's choice rather than mine: re-cut the trailer so that what remains is appropriate for a pre-watershed audience, or move it to a post-watershed break. Within the pre-watershed band the placement constraints below also apply.

If the channel operated mandatory daytime protection the watershed would be disapplied for the channel [UK-SCH-007, UK-FLM-003], but whether any access control applies is expressly unknown, a music channel carrying advertising breaks is an improbable candidate, and the trailer-specific concerns - that viewers do not choose to watch trailers and meet them unawares - are not obviously answered by a gate the viewer has already passed. basis.why: Trailers shown before the watershed for post-watershed programmes must contain only material appropriate for pre-watershed broadcast, and viewers do not choose to watch trailers. The trailer's content as recorded - decayed faces shown in detail, and a pursuit cut faster than in the source - is the material that made the full work a post-watershed proposition, so it is not appropriate for a 15:00 break.

Bright_line and decisive: the trailer does not inherit the 22:15 permission. The practical trap the rule's own note describes is exactly this file - a compliant showing generates a trailer that runs in a daytime break and breaches, with no change to the material.

Supplies the reason and extends the restriction: because trailers are unannounced, viewers come across them unawares, so a pre-watershed trailer must contain ONLY pre-watershed-appropriate material; and trailers kept away from children's programmes should also be kept away from sport and family entertainment, which attract significant child audiences. The programme the 15:00 break sits inside is expressly unknown, so the adjacency limb cannot be assessed and may add a further constraint on any re-cut version.
The standard the pre-watershed appropriateness test is measured against: material unsuitable for children should not in general be shown before 21:00. 15:00 is mid-afternoon, deep inside that band.

Children must be protected by appropriate scheduling from material unsuitable for them. 15:00 on a music channel is a slot where children may be present in numbers, and the appropriate-scheduling factors cannot be run properly because the surrounding programme and its audience profile are unknown.

Here the occult rule's SECOND limb does real work, unlike at 22:15: programmes treating occult or paranormal activity as entertainment must not be broadcast when significant numbers of children may be expected to be watching. That is an audience test rather than a clock test, and a 15:00 break is squarely where it bites. The first limb (presented as real) remains unengaged because the material is fictional. The exemption for drama, film and comedy would matter here if it reached music videos - it names three categories and does not name this one - so I flag it as an open question whose resolution affects how much weight this rule carries, while noting that the trailer rules bar the 15:00 placement independently of it.

Clear information about content that may distress some children should be given, if appropriate, taking account of context - and its own framing is on programmes broadcast BEFORE the watershed, which is this transmission. The observations record that whether the trailer carries the opening disclaimer the full video carries is unknown, and that no warning or signposting is recorded for either showing. Information is not a cure for inappropriate pre-watershed content, but its absence removes even the partial mitigation that might otherwise be weighed.

other_restrictions.requirement: Even on a re-cut trailer, placement constraints survive: trailers restricted away from children's programmes should also be kept away from sport and family entertainment, which draw significant child audiences. The programme the 15:00 break sits inside is expressly unknown, so this cannot be checked. Whether the trailer carries the full video's opening disclaimer is unknown, and no warning or signposting is recorded. For a 30-second trailer an information-based mitigation is close to unavailable in practice: a warning's effectiveness depends on frequency and positioning, and it should convey severity rather than mere presence, neither of which is realistically achievable inside 30 unannounced seconds. This is recorded so that nobody credits the disclaimer with mitigation it has not been shown to carry - and note that the disclaimer, being content supplied by the work itself, is evidence to be weighed rather than a self-clearance.

decisions.reasoning:
ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS. Checked as for t1 and none bites: UK-GEN-001's 'seriously impair' tier is not reached by fictional prosthetic horror with no recorded violence, injury detail or blood (provisional, judgment_based, flagged); UK-SEX-001 and UK-FLM-006 are not engaged; UK-FLM-001 is not engaged because no certificate was sought, which is not a refusal. Note that these prohibitions are absolute in both directions: the trailer's problem is a scheduling problem, not a prohibition, so the correct output is a bar on this slot with routes forward, not a refusal of the material.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE DECISION. UK-TRL-002 is bright_line: trailers are caught by the under-eighteens scheduling rules in their own right and do not inherit the advertised programme's permission. The observations record two transmissions and the extractor expressly states that o8 to o10 are the trailer's events, while also flagging that the schema cannot link an observation to a transmission and that the trailer's timecodes collide numerically with the video's ('00:05' appears for both o3/o4 and o8/o9) while referring to different material. I have kept them apart on that stated mapping.

THE CONTENT OF THE TRAILER, WHICH IS THE POINT. o8 and o9 record that the trailer includes the graveyard sequence WITH the decayed faces - the material the observations describe as shown in detail over an extended sequence in the full work. o10 records the pursuit CUT FASTER than in the full video. So the trailer does not sample the mild parts of the work: it takes the two most distressing sequences and compresses them. UK-TRL-001 requires a pre-watershed trailer to contain ONLY material appropriate for a pre-watershed audience, and UK-TRL-003 explains why the standard is strict - viewers do not choose to watch trailers and come across them unawares, which removes the audience's ability to self-manage that a signposted programme allows. On that standard a 15:00 placement fails.

THE OCCULT RULE'S SECOND LIMB. At 22:15 UK-OCC-001 was satisfied on any reading. At 15:00 the entertainment limb - occult or paranormal activity treated as entertainment must not be broadcast when significant numbers of children may be expected to be watching - is engaged on its own terms, because it is keyed to the expected audience rather than to the clock, and mid-afternoon on a music channel is where that audience sits. The exemption for drama, film and comedy does not name music videos, so whether it reaches this work is a live question; I note that the trailer rules bar this placement independently, so the answer does not hinge on it, but a reviewer should settle it because it affects how the second limb is weighed.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING. I am not refusing the material: a re-cut trailer, or the same cut in a post-watershed break, are both available and are recorded as routes forward. Nor am I clearing it on the strength of the full video's permission, which is the inheritance error. And I am not treating the work's own on-screen disclaimer as a clearance - it is content supplied by the asset, to be weighed as evidence of a fictional framing, and in any event whether the trailer even carries it is unknown.

WHAT CANNOT BE DECIDED. The programme the 15:00 break sits inside, and the age profile of its audience, are expressly unknown, so the adjacency limb of UK-TRL-003 cannot be run and no re-cut version can be fully cleared without it. How often the trailer runs, whether any +1 service carries it, the calendar date and the school-holiday position are all unknown.

CONFLICTS. None arose; no rank-1 rule assists this transmission on the facts recorded.

DETERMINACY AND ESCALATION. UK-TRL-002 is bright_line and settles that this is its own decision. UK-TRL-003 is conditional on adjacency facts not supplied, and the appropriateness judgement runs through judgment_based rules (UK-TRL-001, UK-SCH-001, UK-SCH-005, UK-DEF-002, UK-DEF-003, UK-FLM-010, UK-SCH-010, UK-SCH-011, UK-CTX-010, UK-WRN-002, UK-WRN-003, UK-GEN-001, UK-GEN-002). Two features of the record pull this way: the work contains three distinct menace sequences across 13 minutes (transformation, graveyard, pursuit and cornering), which is arguably 'repeated'; and the pursuit and cornering of a woman by the risen figures (o5) is psychological violence, which the category expressly reaches. decisions.axis_note: France shows all three axes doing different work on the same 22:15 slot. The classification axis issues a real category and it is unsettled between II and III [FR-CLS-002, FR-CLS-003]. The hours axis is NOT a function of the category alone: on II there is no clock rule at all and the constraint is placement [FR-SCH-001]; on III the hour depends on the service - 22:00 on other services, Wednesdays-before-20:30 on cinema channels and pay-per-view [FR-SCH-002, FR-SCH-003]; and on IV the same category yields 22:30 on one service type and 20:30 on another, a two-hour spread with identical content [FR-SCH-005, FR-SCH-006]. That is the French pattern the three-axis design exists to capture, and it is the reason a single 'the rating is X so the time is Y' answer would be wrong here even though France does issue ratings. The third axis is purely CUMULATIVE: pictogram for the whole duration, written mention, press-schedule information and the trailer obligations all sit on top of the window and none of them buys an earlier hour [FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002, FR-SIG-003, FR-TRL-001]. decisions.reasoning:
ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS FIRST, read for coverage rather than category label, because every one of them is a judgment_based row and a label-driven read would misfire here. FR-LAW-001 bans programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm (nuire gravement) the development of minors, with no time or technical cure; this is tier 1 of a two-tier standard whose tier 2 (FR-LAW-002) covers content liable merely to HARM, which is schedulable with time and/or technical means. A 13-minute fictional horror music video with prosthetic effects, no recorded violence or injury detail and an explicit disclaimer disavowing occult belief is at most tier 2 and probably below it. Provisional view: FR-LAW-001 does not bite; flagged. FR-PRO-002 bans PORNOGRAPHIC programmes depicting under-18s: no sexual content of any kind is recorded, and the prompt's warning is exactly on point - applying this on the strength of its sexual_content key would be absurd here. FR-PRO-001 bans programmes which OFFEND HUMAN DIGNITY, in particular those depicting sexual violence, perversions or degradation, and admits no hour, category or technical cure; nothing in the observations approaches it - the decayed faces are prosthetic effects on fictional risen corpses, not degradation of a person. FR-PRO-003 bans programmes of EXTREME OR GRATUITOUS VIOLENCE outright, and its own note requires it to be distinguished from category V 'very great violence'; the observations record no violence at all in the ordinary sense (the input is expressly silent on whether any violence, injury detail or blood occurs), so it is not engaged. It is judgment_based with human_review_required=yes, so the provisional view is flagged rather than asserted.

ROUTING. is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no'. Two transmissions, decided separately: the video at 22:15 and the 30-second trailer at 15:00. The extractor's stated mapping (o1 to o7 to the video, o8 to o10 to the trailer) is used rather than pooling the observations, and the extractor's warning that the trailer timecodes collide numerically with the video's is respected.

SERVICE APPLICABILITY. The French scheme's timings turn on cinema channel / pay-per-view versus other television services. 'Music channel' is neither of those in terms, the request supplies no service type, and the observations record the channel's commercial model as unknown. I branch and label both limbs. For the provisional II and III classifications 22:15 is permitted either way, which I state plainly; for a IV classification the limb would decide the case.

CLASSIFICATION, AND WHY I DO NOT SETTLE IT. II fits the 'certain scenes liable to shock under-10s' wording for a work with three discrete scare sequences. III is live because its wording expressly reaches programmes liable to disturb under-12s where THE PROGRAMME resorts in a REPEATED way to physical or psychological violence, and three menace sequences in 13 minutes plus a pursuit-and-cornering (which is psychological violence in the rule's own words) is a defensible reading of 'repeated'. There is no cinema visa to anchor either reading - the asset holds no certificate anywhere - so FR-FLM-001's usual indication is absent and the editor's commission de visionnage carries the whole decision. Because the editor assigns the category, and because FR-CLS-003 is judgment_based and already flagged for review, I report II as provisional with III live and price IV as the outcome that would change the answer.

THE HOURS. The striking feature is how much turns on fifteen minutes and on a service label. On category III on other services the window opens at 22:00 and the slot is 22:15. On category IV on other services it opens at 22:30 and the slot would breach. On a cinema channel or pay-per-view service both categories open earlier (Wednesdays-before-20:30 for III, after 20:30 for IV) and 22:15 is comfortable. So the boundaries cluster within half an hour of this start time, and none of them is sensitive to anything about the material: they are sensitive to the category, the service type and the clock. A reviewer moving this slot earlier by twenty minutes, or a classifier moving it up one category, would cross a boundary.

WHAT DOES NOT APPLY. The category V regime - the eligibility gate, the 00:00-05:00 window, the decoder locking specification, the penal-code warning and the elapsed compliance deadlines - is in this slice and is nowhere near engaged; I record it as checked because the slice includes it and an unexplained silence would be indistinguishable from an oversight. FR-VIO-003 requires advance warning for difficult images or testimony concerning particularly dramatic EVENTS, in news and other programmes; on its wording it addresses real events and testimony rather than fictional horror imagery, so I read it as not engaged, while flagging that the rule says 'and other programmes' and a reviewer might read it more broadly - if they did, it would require advance warning rather than move the hour. I record one absence explicitly rather than letting it pass as silence: this slice contains no category-independent rule on how violence or frightening material may be presented during daytime hours, and no general pre-watershed-equivalent route conditioned on educational accompaniment, so every French constraint on the hour here runs through the category-and-service windows.

DETERMINACY AND ESCALATION. FR-SCH-002, FR-SCH-003, FR-SCH-005 and FR-SCH-006 are all bright_line and apply mechanically once the category and the service type are fixed - but both of those inputs are open. FR-CLS-003 is judgment_based with human_review_required=yes, FR-CLS-002 is judgment_based, FR-CV-001 and FR-VIO-003 are conditional, and all four absolute prohibitions are judgment_based. Human review is mandatory. Confidence is medium: 22:15 is permitted on the two most plausible classifications and on both service limbs, but the margin is fifteen minutes on one branch and a IV classification would flip one limb outright.

decisions.reasoning:
ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS. Checked as for the feature and none bites: FR-LAW-001's 'nuire gravement' tier is not reached by 30 seconds of fictional prosthetic horror; FR-PRO-001 (human dignity, in particular sexual violence, perversions or degradation) is not engaged by prosthetic decayed faces on fictional risen corpses; FR-PRO-002 (pornography depicting minors) is plainly not engaged and its sexual_content key must not be mistaken for its scope; FR-PRO-003 (extreme or gratuitous violence) is not engaged on a record that does not describe violence at all, and its own note requires it to be distinguished from category V 'very great violence'. All four are judgment_based and the provisional views are flagged. The trailer's problem is a scheduling and content-standard problem, not a prohibition: the correct output is a bar on this slot with routes forward, not a refusal of the material.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE DECISION. The observations record two transmissions and the extractor states the mapping of observations to each. In France the separation is enforced by the trailer rules themselves: FR-TRL-001 imposes a content standard on the trailer, FR-TRL-002 a placement rule, and FR-TRL-003 a clock rule for category IV trailers which is DIFFERENT from the category IV programme rule (20:30 for the trailer against 22:30 for the programme on non-cinema services). A system that assessed the asset once would miss all three.

THE CONTENT STANDARD, WHICH DECIDES IT. FR-TRL-001 requires that a trailer must NOT contain scenes likely to offend young viewers. The trailer as recorded includes the graveyard sequence WITH the decayed faces (o8, o9) - described in the feature's observations as shown in detail over an extended sequence - and the pursuit cut FASTER than in the full video (o10). The trailer therefore selects the work's most distressing material and intensifies its presentation. That does not meet the standard, and because the standard is a content rule rather than a clock rule it is not answered by the hour, by the feature's permission, or by a mild category.

WHAT THIS SLICE DOES NOT CONTAIN, STATED RATHER THAN PASSED OVER. There is no category-independent French rule here restricting how violence or frightening material may be presented during daytime and early-evening hours - the kind of rule that would say, for instance, that within daytime hours menace must not be perceived as continuous or in an exacerbated form. On a 30-second cut built from a graveyard sequence and a faster-cut pursuit, menace is close to continuous by construction, so such a rule would be the natural second ground for barring this slot, and would also be the answer to anyone arguing that a mild category disposes of the matter. FR-VIO-003 is the only distressing-imagery row supplied and on its wording addresses real events and testimony. I therefore rest the bar on FR-TRL-001 alone, which is bright_line and sufficient, and record the gap so that a reviewer with the full table checks for the second ground rather than reading its absence here as permission.

WHAT A IV CLASSIFICATION WOULD DO. It would make the answer trivial: FR-TRL-003 bars category IV trailers before 20:30 outright. I price that branch rather than relying on it, since IV is not my provisional view.

WHAT CANNOT BE DECIDED. The programme the 15:00 break sits inside, and the age profile of its audience, are expressly unknown, so FR-TRL-002's proximity-to-children's-programmes limb cannot be run and no re-cut version can be fully cleared without it. Whether the trailer carries any signage or the work's disclaimer is unknown. How often the trailer runs, whether any timeshift carriage exists, and the calendar date are all unknown. And the classification itself is unsettled between II and III, which changes whether FR-TRL-002's bright-line proximity rule applies or only a 'particular care' standard.

CONFLICTS. None arose. The rank-1 rows (FR-LAW-001, FR-LAW-002) do not assist this transmission; FR-LAW-002's framework of time and/or technical means is consistent with the rank-2 rules being the operative instruments.

DETERMINACY AND ESCALATION. FR-TRL-001, FR-TRL-002 and FR-TRL-003 are bright_line, which is why the conclusion that the described cut cannot run at 15:00 is firm. But the classification feeding them is unsettled and judgment_based (FR-CLS-002, FR-CLS-003 with human_review_required=yes), FR-VIO-003 is conditional and its scope is a matter of reading, the four absolute prohibitions are judgment_based, and FR-TRL-002's placement limb cannot be checked at all. cross_country_note: Four decisions, two countries, two transmissions, one piece of material - and the instructive divergences run in two different directions at once. ON THE CLASSIFICATION AXIS the countries are mirror images: the UK issues no per-programme rating for linear television and the asset holds no certificate anywhere [UK-FLM-010], while France issues a real per-programme category which here is unsettled between II (-10) and III (-12) and is assigned by the editor's own commission de visionnage [FR-CLS-002, FR-CLS-003]. ON THE 22:15 SHOWING both countries permit it, but for structurally different reasons: the UK because 22:15 is past a single bright-line watershed [UK-SCH-002], France because a category II work has no clock restriction at all [FR-SCH-001] or, on a III classification, because 22:15 clears a 22:00 window on other services and the Wednesday-20:30 rule on cinema channels and pay-per-view [FR-SCH-002, FR-SCH-003]. The French margin is fifteen minutes on one branch, and a category IV classification would split the French answer by service type alone - barred at 22:15 on other television services (22:30) but permitted on cinema channels and pay-per-view (20:30) [FR-SCH-005, FR-SCH-006] - which is a two-hour spread on identical content and has no UK analogue. ON THE 15:00 TRAILER both countries refuse the described cut, and here the mechanisms are worth distinguishing because they fail differently. The UK reaches it through the trailer rules: a trailer is caught by the scheduling rules in its own right and does not inherit the feature's permission, viewers meet trailers unawares, and a pre-watershed trailer may contain only pre-watershed-appropriate material [UK-TRL-001, UK-TRL-002, UK-TRL-003]. France reaches it through a single bright-line content standard on the trailer itself: a trailer must not contain scenes likely to offend young viewers [FR-TRL-001], which a 30-second concentrate built from the decayed faces and a faster-cut pursuit does not satisfy. The difference in mechanism matters for anyone extending this system: the UK bar is a scheduling judgement measured against the watershed, so it moves with the hour, while the French bar is a content standard that does not reference the clock at all, so re-timing the trailer does not answer it and only a re-cut or the category IV clock rule [FR-TRL-003] would. The French route is also the more striking of the two, because it holds even on the MOST PERMISSIVE classification: a category II feature has no clock restriction whatever, and its trailer still cannot run at 15:00. That is the clearest demonstration in this whole case that the rating does not determine the hours - in the country that actually issues ratings. THREE ASYMMETRIES WORTH RECORDING. First, the UK has a rule directly on point for this content and France does not: UK-OCC-001 addresses occult and paranormal material with a three-way split (presented as real, entertainment, fiction exempt), and no French rule in the slice addresses the occult at all - though the UK rule's fiction exemption is enumerated as 'drama, film and comedy' and does not name music videos, which is an open question flagged in both UK decisions. Second, France's signage obligations are bright-line and heavy for a 13-minute work - pictogram throughout, a written mention of at least 1 minute at the bottom of screen or 12 seconds full-screen, classification in trailers and press schedules [FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002, FR-SIG-003] - where the UK slice has only judgment-based warning-adequacy standards [UK-WRN-002, UK-WRN-003] and, for pre-watershed showings, a discretionary information duty [UK-SCH-005]. Third, France gives the TRAILER its own clock rule that differs from the programme's (category IV trailers barred before 20:30 while the programme waits until 22:30 on non-cinema services) [FR-TRL-003], a divergence between asset and derived asset that the UK expresses as a general 'assessed in its own slot' standard rather than as two different numbers. On the absolute prohibitions both countries land the same way for the same reason - 'seriously impair' and 'nuire gravement' are a higher tier than ordinary harm, and 13 minutes of fictional prosthetic horror with no recorded violence or injury detail is not in it [UK-GEN-001, FR-LAW-001, FR-LAW-002] - but every one of those rows is judgment_based, the observations expressly do not say whether any violence, injury detail or blood occurs, and so all four decisions flag the point rather than resting on it.
